items.text: Geometric properties over a field

Absolute properties of $X$ over $k$ (reduced, connected, irreducible) are not stable under $X_{k'}$; the geometric property: true for $X$ over $k$ iff true for $X_{k'}$ for every extension $k'$ of $k$ (take $k'$ algebraically closed).
Perfect fields
For a field $k$ the following are equivalent:
(a) $k$ is perfect; (b) $A,B$ reduced $k$-algebras $\Rightarrow$ $A\otimes_k B$ reduced;
(c) $A$ reduced $\Rightarrow$ $A\otimes_k k'$ reduced for every extension $k'$; (d) $k'\otimes_k k'$ reduced for every finite purely inseparable $k'/k$.
Perfect: $\operatorname{char}k=0$, or $\operatorname{char}k=p$ and $x\mapsto x^p$ is surjective. (b)$\Rightarrow$(c)$\Rightarrow$(d) are particular cases.
(d)\Rightarrow(a):\ x\notin k^p,\quad k'=k[t]/(t^p-x),\qquad k'\otimes_k k'\simeq k'[t]/(t^p-x)=k'[t]/(t-\alpha)^p\ \text{not reduced}
(a)$\Rightarrow$(b): $K,L$ extensions of the perfect field $k$ $\Rightarrow$ $K\otimes_k L$ reduced (admitted); $A,B$ reduced embed in products of fields.
Geometrically reduced (separable) algebras
$A$ a $k$-algebra, $K_1$ a perfect extension of $k$ (e.g. the perfect closure $k^{p^{-\infty}}$). Equivalent:
(a) $A\otimes_k B$ reduced for every reduced $k$-algebra $B$; (b) $A\otimes_k k'$ reduced for every extension $k'$;
(c) $A\otimes_k K_1$ reduced; (d) $A\otimes_k k'$ reduced for every finite radicial $k'$ (of degree $p$).
Then $A$ is geometrically reduced, or separable over $k$.
(c)\Rightarrow(b):\ A_{k'}\subset A_{K_1'}=(A\otimes K_1)\otimes_{K_1}K_1',\quad K_1\ \text{perfect}
(d)\Rightarrow(c):\ K_1=k^{p^{-\infty}}=\varinjlim k_i,\quad A\otimes K_1=\varinjlim A\otimes k_i\ \text{reduced}
Separable schemes

$X$ over $k$: (a) $X\times_k Y$ reduced for all reduced $Y$; (b) $X_{k'}$ reduced for all $k'$; (c) $X_{K_1}$ reduced; (d) $X_{k'}$ reduced for finite radicial $k'$. Equivalent (reduce to affine); then $X$ is geometrically reduced or separable over $k$.
Separable $\Rightarrow$ reduced; the converse holds for all $X$ iff $k$ is perfect. $X$ separable over $k$ $\iff$ $X_{k'}$ separable over $k'$.
Separably closed fields
For a field $k$ the following are equivalent: (a) $k$ separably closed (every finite Galois extension trivial);
(b) $A,B$ with $\operatorname{Spec}$ irreducible $\Rightarrow$ $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_k B)$ irreducible, i.e. $A\otimes B/\mathrm{nil}$ is a domain;
(c) $A$ a domain, $k'/k$ an extension $\Rightarrow$ $A_{k'}/\mathrm{nil}$ is a domain; (d) $k'\otimes_k k'$ is a domain for every finite Galois $k'/k$.
(d)\Rightarrow(a):\ k'/k\ \text{Galois with group }\Gamma:\quad k'\otimes_k k'\simeq\prod_{\Gamma}k'
(a)$\Rightarrow$(b): reduce to fields $K,L$ over $k$ separably closed: $K\otimes_k L/\mathrm{nil}$ is a domain (classical, admitted).
Geometrically irreducible schemes
$X$ over $k$, $K_1$ a separably closed extension. Equivalent: (a) $X\times_k Y$ irreducible for all irreducible $Y$; (b) $X_{k'}$ irreducible for all $k'$;
(c) $X_{K_1}$ irreducible; (d) $X_{k'}$ irreducible for every finite Galois $k'/k$. Then $X$ is geometrically irreducible.
(b)$\Rightarrow$(a): $Y=\bigcup Y_i$ non-empty affine opens meeting pairwise; reduce to $Y$ and $X$ affine and $Y$ integral.
X=\operatorname{Spec}A,\ Y=\operatorname{Spec}B:\quad A\otimes_k B\subset A\otimes_k \operatorname{Frac}(B)
(c)$\Rightarrow$(b): $X_{K_1'}\to X_{k'}$ is surjective, and a continuous image of an irreducible space is irreducible.
K_1=k_{\mathrm{sep}}=\varinjlim k_i\ (k_i/k\ \text{finite Galois}),\qquad X_{K_1}=\varprojlim X_{k_i}\ \text{(affine over }X)
(d)\Rightarrow(c):\ A_{k_i}\ \text{reduced (since }k_i/k\ \text{separable) and}\ A_{k_i}/\mathrm{nil}\ \text{a domain, so a domain;}\quad A_{K_1}=\varinjlim A_{k_i}\ \text{a domain}
Geometrically irreducible $\Rightarrow$ irreducible; the converse holds for all $X$ iff $k$ is separably closed. $X$ geometrically irreducible over $k$ $\iff$ $X_{k'}$ over $k'$.
